title: Human-induced climate change compounded by socio-economic water stressors increased severity of 5-year drought…
methodology: SPEI, rainfall analysis, non-stationary extreme-value methods and vulnerability synthesis
limitations: Rapid attribution analysis; rainfall attribution uncertainty includes no change; some vulnerability statements synthesize secondary sources. (World Weather Attribution)

title: Anthropogenic drought dominates groundwater depletion in Iran
methodology: Groundwater observations, recharge, withdrawal, return flows, precipitation and evaporation
limitations: Historical period; does not measure contemporary FCV outcomes. (Nature)

title: Islamic Republic of Iran Intended Nationally Determined Contribution
organization: National Climate Change Committee of Iran / UNFCCC repository
methodology: Government policy statements and national projections
limitations: Government-authored; some projection methodology is not stated in the accessible text; original UNFCCC file endpoint was inaccessible during verification. (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

title: Iran Economic Monitor, Spring 2022: Managing Economic Uncertainties
methodology: Macroeconomic assessment; special section on uncertain water future
limitations: Publication page verified; full report was not accessible through the browsing endpoint, so only webpage claims are used. (World Bank)

title: Islamic Republic of Iran country overview
limitations: Economic synthesis rather than causal climate study; conflict-related statements should be attributed to the World Bank. (World Bank)

title: Iran, Islamic Rep. - World Development Indicators
limitations: Indicators have different reference years and underlying methodologies. (World Bank Open Data)

title: Impact of climate change on water crisis and conflicts: Farmers’ perceptions at the ZayandehRud Basin in Iran
organization: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies / Elsevier
methodology: Meteorological records + random survey of 301 farmers
limitations: Open-access 2024 farmer-perception study; local ZayandehRud Basin findings do not establish national or causal conflict effects.

title: UNDP Iran CIWP Factsheet
geographic_coverage: Lake Urmia, Shadegan, Bakhtegan, Parishan, Anzali and participating villages
limitations: No independent counterfactual; performance figures are programme-reported. (UNDP)

title: Conservation of Iranian Wetlands Project - Phase II (Scale-up)
limitations: Achievement statements are implementing-agency reports, not independent impact evaluation. (UNDP)

title: Terminal Evaluation consultancy notice - Lake Urmia and other wetlands
limitations: Demonstrates commissioning of an evaluation, not its findings; final evaluation report not verified. (UNGM)

title: FAO and Iran launch regional project to strengthen climate-resilient agriculture
limitations: Describes intended activities, not evaluated outcomes; agriculture-water statistic differs from WWA terminology. (FAOHome)

title: Projects - FAO in Iran
limitations: Budgets and timeframes demonstrate committed/programmed capacity, not effectiveness. (FAOHome)

title: Iran's Khuzestan: Thirst and Turmoil
temporal_coverage: 2021 protests and preceding water-sector conditions, reported in 2023
methodology: Accessible publisher summary describes the Khuzestan protest and water-scarcity analysis; detailed methods are not stated there.
limitations: The canonical publisher page returned 403; claims are limited to the indexed publisher summary, not full-report detail.

title: Iran's water policy: Environmental injustice and peripheral marginalisation
temporal_coverage: Historical and contemporary water-transfer policy, as discussed in 2024
methodology: Qualitative content analysis of policy and government documents, campaigns and Persian-, Kurdish- and English-language secondary material.
limitations: Interpretive analysis; documents and reported examples do not quantify causal effects of individual transfers.

title: The politics of drought in the Middle East, case study from Iran
temporal_coverage: Recent drought politics, compared across two provinces in a 2025 study
methodology: Comparative qualitative case analysis of drought politics in Isfahan and Hamedan.
limitations: The author notes limited prior research and calls for further regional and media-perception analysis.

title: Groundwater resources exploitation management in response to water scarcity challenges in Khuzestan Province, Iran
organization: Journal of Groundwater Science and Engineering
temporal_coverage: Groundwater measurements from 2008-2018; article published in 2025
methodology: Groundwater-level and hydrochemical analysis of204exploration wells and70piezometric wells across19aquifers; observed data2008–2018.
limitations: Well observations cover 2008-2018; findings do not measure current household access or climate attribution.
